content.heading: A language for the work ahead.
content.body: A general-purpose programming language and toolchain built around one challenge: make useful software easier to write, understand, run, and deliver.
content.caption: Programming, re-examined
An editorial paraphrase of the project's own north-star question, not a quotation.

content.heading: Packages and ecosystem
content.body: Guion can call Python libraries such as NumPy through a typed bridge, and the packages tested so far work. Broad package compatibility is still open, so for a project that leans on many libraries, Python is the safer choice today.
content.caption: Packages and ecosystem
content.note: The bridge is an explicit typed call. It is not transparent Python compatibility.

content.heading: Calling NumPy from Guion
content.body: On the one 100,000-row task measured, Guion took 1.025 times as long as the same function called from Python.
content.caption: Calling NumPy from Guion
content.note: Sending raw bytes instead of text closed most of the gap. Not all of it.

content.heading: A release you can use
content.body: No public Guion release has been published. Python is a released language with a long track record.
content.caption: A release you can use
content.note: Guion is in active development. It has been validated on macOS ARM64 and on Debian 12 for ARM64 and x86_64. No other target is claimed.

content.heading: Learning it
content.body: Whether a new builder can learn Guion, find its APIs and make a realistic change from the guides is still being tested.
content.caption: Learning it
content.note: Learnability is listed as an open outcome on the project status page.

content.heading: Beyond the tasks measured
content.body: Every number on this page is for a named program on a named machine against a named Python version. The server results come from one run on each of two cloud machines; an Intel Xeon server measured Guion slower on an earlier build and has not been rerun. Free-threaded Python and PyPy were not compared.
content.caption: Beyond the tasks measured
content.note: Overall competitiveness remains open, in the project's own words.

content.heading: Absence is a value
content.body: maybe_positive(-5) comes back as None, and the program tests is_some before it prints.
content.caption: option.gu
content.note: A function that can come back empty says so in its type, so the reader knows to check.
